thread.title: Universal Display Duel: JPMorgan Says Wait, Goldman Sees Nice Setup

author: Barron's
title: Universal Display Duel: JPMorgan Says Wait, Goldman Sees Nice Setup
text:
Shares of organic light-emitting diode technology maker Universal Display ( OLED ) are holding on to gains following a report by Korea's Electronic Times speculating that Apple ( AAPL ) will use OLEDs in screens of three different iPhones in 2019, based on comments from multiple unnamed sources from the industry.
Shares of Universal are up $7.02, or 7%, at $106.67. Apple stock is down 33 cents at $188.24.
Universal Display Corp. Universal's stock has been in a slump this year as analysts concluded that sales of the OLED-based iPhone X were disappointing, and that as a consequence, Apple will not extend OLED this year to its other models for the fall lineup. Even with today's jump, Universal stock is down 38% so far in 2018.
There's something of a duel today , however, about the prospects for Universal, between JPMorgan 's Jay Kwon and Goldman Sachs 's Brian Lee .
Kwon thinks this report is a "false alarm," according to a summary of the research provided by TheFlyonTheWall . (JPMorgan declined to provide the comments directly to me.) According to TheFly's summary, Kwon thinks it "highly unlikely" that Apple would use OLED across an entire lineup of iPhones next year. Rather, Kwon says, Apple will use OLED in two, not three, iPhone models in 2019, with one model sticking with an LCD-based display.
Kwon also argues it is too early for Apple to have reached such a decision. And even if it were true, he writes, the current supply of OLED technology out there is enough for another 50 million additional units of smartphones. Kwon's implication would seem to be that the upside of new sales would be limited for Universal.
On the brighter side, Goldman's Lee reiterates a Buy rating, and a $150 price target, after reflecting on "data points" from a couple conferences he's been following, the DisplayWeek conference last week and Goldman's own Technet conference.
The first quarter of this year was "the trough" for Universal, Lee believes, and even though inventory remains a "hangover" for Universal this quarter, it will be "less impactful quarter over quarter," he writes. Also, Samsung Electronics ( 005930.Korea ), Universal's biggest customer, historically, is likely to increase purchases from Universal this quarter, he notes.
In addition to Samsung, LG Electronics ( 066570.Korea ) is becoming a bigger part of the business, notes Lee. "At 55% of sales in 1Q, the level of LG revenue contribution for OLED hit a new record and would appear to be on track to grow 20%-30% yoy on the back of TVs alone," writes Lee.
In sum, "we continue to see an attractive setup into 2H18 given tepid investor sentiment despite the potential for normalizing materials volume trends at Samsung starting in 3Q, continued strength in TVs, and mid-to-long term upside in blue, among other factors."
